newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end mostly lower as wheat slides.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end mostly lower as wheat slides.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures closed mostly lower on a sharp break in wheat and lower corn futures, traders said.
"The world numbers were bearish for everything except beans and beans want to go higher. But wheat is struggling just as it did all last week," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds.

Soybeans moved on both sides of Tuesday's settlement levels and new crop November closed above key support at the $8.00 per bushel mark. The market again was volatile with November swinging in a 14-1/2 cent per bushel range.

USDA early Wednesday pegged 1996 U.S. soybean production at 2.27 billion bushels, above an average of analysts' estimates for 2.24 billion but below USDA's forecast in August for 2.3 billion bushels. USDA also cut its estimate for 1996-97 U.S. soybean carryout to 160 million bushels, down from the August forecast for 175 million.
Forecasts for cool weather to soon move into the U.S. Midwest also underpinned the soybean market and nearby September closed higher.
Soybeans closed 1-1/2 cents per bushel higher to 2-3/4 lower, with November down two at $8.05 a bushel.
"Grains were weaker but beans hung in there. The weather is supportive for beans," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.

Meteorologists early Wednesday said a cold front was moving across the western U.S. Midwest Wednesday and was expected to push eastward during the week, bringing below normal temperatures to the corn/soy belt.

"There is some chilly weather around," said Mike Palmerino, meteorologist with Weather Services Corp. "It appears as though it is going to be moving across the Midwest in the next couple of days." Low temperatures were expected in the 40s Farenheit in the western corn belt Thursday and Friday mornings with some 30s F possible in Minnesota and northern Iowa, he said.
Sources said the cool weather could hamper pod filling in late-planted soybeans.
Refco Inc bought eight million bushels of November and sold seven million, traders said, while Rosenthal Collins bought seven million November and sold three million.
Cargill Inc sold 3.0 million bushels of November and Cargill Investor Services sold 2.5 million November, traders said.
Soybean futures volume was estimated at 60,000, up from 48,905 Tuesday, according to the CBOT.

In soybean options, Lind Waldock bought 2,000 January $7.50 puts and sold 2,000 November $7.50 puts at 5-1/2 to 5-1/4 cents, sources said. Continental Grain bought 800 January $8.25 calls and sold 800 January $9.25 calls at 22-3/4 to 23 cents, they said.
Soybean options volume was estimated at 35,000, down from 36,229 Tuesday.
